issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Bitmap24: the template header declares a three-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) but the implementation (in the template .cpp) defines a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses the two-parameter constructor in both header and implementation. This inconsistency in the template (header vs implementation) will cause compile-time errors and confuse students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template header and implementation consistent. Either (A) change template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) to match the .cpp implementation, or (B) implement a matching three-parameter constructor Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) in Bitmap24.cpp. Prefer option (A) because the solution and existing implementation expect the two-parameter constructor.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor declaration in the template header disagrees with its implementation and with the solution header: template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) (an extra 'depth' parameter) while the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp defines a two-argument constructor Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses the two-argument declaration (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)). This mismatch (extra parameter name/presence) creates confusion for students: the header in the template does not match the implementation they must work with and differs from the reference solution, which can prevent compilation and force students to spend time reconciling the inconsistent API rather than focusing on the assignment logic.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template header match the implementation and the solution: change the constructor declaration in template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (remove the extraneous 'int depth' parameter). This aligns template, implementation, and solution and avoids compilation/API confusion for students.
